keyTakeaways: An engagement gift for a couple splits into four situations - a guest, family at a sagai or roka, the bride giving to the groom, and the groom giving to the bride - and only two of the four are answered by a romantic keepsake.

India's Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents) Rules, 1985, in force since 2 October 1985, require the bride and the bridegroom each to keep a written, signed list of presents given at the time of the marriage, with every giver's name and each present's approximate value.

Givers misread price in a measurable direction: in a 216-participant 2025 experiment, 22.22% of people in the giver role thought a premium-priced gift would move the recipient more, against 59.72% of people in the recipient role.
The digital bouquet is SubhSandesh's #2 page type at 801 of 3,417 pages (23.4%), and 50.2% of all shared-page views happen on a phone (21,101 of 42,017).

A shareable page is the wrong engagement gift in three cases: when the two families are exchanging presents formally, when you are attending in person, and when the recipient is not comfortable on a smartphone.

faqs.question: Is a cash envelope an acceptable engagement gift?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the most useful thing you can hand over, because it lets the couple decide. The trade-off is that it is the least memorable option and nobody keeps the envelope. If you go this route, put something written alongside it so there is a record of who gave what and why.

faqs.question: Do I still give a wedding gift if I already gave an engagement gift?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the usual pattern. Treat the engagement present as the small one and keep the larger one for the wedding, rather than spending your whole budget at the first event. If you are choosing between the two, the wedding gift is the one people notice the absence of.

faqs.question: Is it rude to give the bride and the groom separate gifts instead of one for the couple?
faqs.answer: Not rude, but it reads differently. A single gift for the two of them signals that you are congratulating a couple; two separate gifts signal that you have a relationship with each of them individually. Guests almost always do better with one shared present.

faqs.question: Can a group of friends give one engagement gift together?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually buys something better than five separate small gifts. A group gift also solves the awkwardness of very different budgets inside a friend circle. Name everyone on the card or the page so the couple know who to thank.

faqs.question: What should I write in an engagement card if I barely know the couple?
faqs.answer: Congratulate them on the engagement rather than on the marriage, name whichever of the two you actually know, and stop. Two honest sentences beat a paragraph of borrowed sentiment. Avoid predictions about the wedding date, which they may not have settled.

faqs.question: Is it too late to send an engagement gift a month afterwards?
faqs.answer: No. Engagements have no gift deadline the way a wedding day does, and a late present with a real message lands better than a rushed one. If you have missed the ceremony entirely, sending something that acknowledges you were not there is more graceful than pretending otherwise.

faqs.question: Is jewellery a safe engagement gift for someone else's couple?
faqs.answer: It is a risky choice from a guest. Jewellery at an Indian betrothal usually flows between the two families rather than from guests, so a guest's jewellery gift can read as stepping into a family exchange. If you are not family, choose something that does not carry that meaning.

faqs.question: What if the couple already live together and own everything?
faqs.answer: Then an object is the wrong category, because they have solved the object problem themselves. Give something that records rather than equips: photographs, a written page, a booking for something they will do together. This is the case where a keepsake genuinely outperforms a household item.

faqs.question: Should an engagement gift have both their names on it?
faqs.answer: Both names work for anything the two of them will share, and one name works for anything private. Personalising a shared gift with only one name is the most common mistake here. If you are unsure of a spelling, ask rather than guess.

faqs.question: How do I stop a digital engagement gift from being seen before the ceremony?
faqs.answer: Put a password on it before you share the link. On SubhSandesh, 42.7% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it (1,458 of 3,417), which is the mechanism for exactly this. Remember the recipient then needs the password from you, so send it separately and not in the same message.

faqs.question: Do engagement gifts need to be given in person?
faqs.answer: No, and for anyone outside the city it is often better not to try. 50.2% of shared SubhSandesh page views happen on a phone (21,101 of 42,017), so a link reaches the recipient with nothing needed at their end. If you are in the room, though, something to hand over beats something to open on a screen.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Engagement Gift for Couple: Four Situations, Not One

An engagement gift for couple is really four different gifts wearing one name, and the register changes completely depending on who is giving. A guest brings something small and shared. Close family at an Indian sagai or roka are inside a family-to-family exchange that Indian law treats differently from a guest's present.

The bride and the groom, giving to each other, are in the most private register of the four, and the only one where a personal keepsake is unambiguously right. SubhSandesh has recorded 3,417 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12 across 15 page types, and the digital bouquet accounts for 801 of them, 23.4% of everything built. Below: the four situations sorted, what the Dowry Prohibition Rules, 1985 require of presents at a marriage, and where price instinct goes wrong.

## What is an engagement gift?

An engagement gift is a present marking a betrothal — the agreement to marry — rather than the marriage itself. By convention it is smaller and less formal than a wedding gift, because the wedding is where the heavier giving happens. That convention is widely followed rather than written down anywhere.

Indian law does not recognise the betrothal at all. The [Hindu Marriage Act, 1955](https://indiacode.gov.in/handle/123456789/531350), enacted 18 May 1955, runs to 37 sections: section 5 sets the conditions for a marriage, and section 7 provides that where the rites include the Saptapadi, the marriage "becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken". Not one section mentions an engagement or a betrothal.

So a sagai, roka or mangni carries real social weight and no legal standing. That is part of why the gift does so much work — it is often the only thing anyone keeps.

## Do you have to send an engagement gift?

No. An engagement gift is optional in a way a wedding gift is not. Turning up, calling, or sending a message is the obligation; the object is a choice.

Three things move the answer, and the size of the guest list is not one of them. First, whether this is a joint ceremony with guests or a family-only roka, where a guest present sits oddly.

Second, whether you are giving to the couple or to one of them, because those are separate registers with separate budgets. Third, whether a wedding gift is still coming from you later, since that is where the heavier giving is expected.

If you send nothing, send something written. Across 42,017 recorded views of shared SubhSandesh pages — 12.3 per page on average — a link tends to reach more people than a parcel does.

## Four engagement-gift situations, and what each one needs

Sort yourself into one of these before you shop. The situation matters more than the object.

### 1. A friend or colleague at the engagement party

You are a guest. The register is small, shared, and clearly not competing with the wedding gift you will give later — something for the two of them together rather than for one of them. This is where most engagement gift ideas for friends land, and where a shared keepsake, such as a page of photographs from before they met each other's families, does more than an object destined for a cupboard.

### 2. Close family at a sagai or roka

This is not guest gifting. Presents flowing between the two families at an Indian betrothal sit inside a much older exchange, and they are the ones Indian law has an opinion about.

If you are a parent, sibling or uncle here, ask what the two families have agreed rather than choosing on your own. A romantic keepsake page is the wrong answer, and so is a surprise.

### 3. An engagement gift for the bride, from the groom

Private, personal, and the only situation where sentiment is the entire brief. Nobody else sees it. A hand-tied [digital bouquet you build bloom by bloom](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) is the second-most-created thing on SubhSandesh at 801 pages, 23.4% of everything, and it exists for exactly this register: pick the flowers, write the card, send a link that opens when she taps it.

### 4. An engagement gift for the groom, from the bride

Same register, and the one people find hardest. The mistake is copying the guest playbook and buying an object; what works is the record — what you thought when you met him, what you told your mother that night.

The [romantic "I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) is the most-created template on the platform at 1,001 pages, 29.3% of all creations. The median gap between a creator's first save and last edit on one is 6.9 hours (n=1,001), which says people go away and come back rather than firing it off.

### 5. Anyone sending from another city or country

Distance changes the object, not the gesture. 50.2% of shared page views happen on a phone (21,101 of 42,017), so a link needs nothing at the far end but the phone already in their hand.

If the proposal itself has not happened yet, the ["Will You Marry Me?" proposal scrapbook](https://subhsandesh.in/proposal) is the page built for that moment instead.

Here is how the situations sit side by side, against SubhSandesh's own numbers:

| Situation | Who gives | Register | Platform signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engagement party guest | Friend, colleague, cousin | Small, shared, not extravagant | 42,017 views across 3,417 pages, 12.3 per page |
| Sagai or roka, family side | Parents, siblings, uncles | Family-to-family, agreed in advance | 0 of 15 page types address a family exchange |
| For the bride, from the groom | The groom alone | Private, sentimental | Digital bouquet: 801 pages, 23.4% of all creations |
| For the groom, from the bride | The bride alone | Private, sentimental | "I love you" page: 1,001 pages, 29.3%, 6.9-hour median edit gap |
| Sending from another city | Anyone | Whatever survives the distance | 50.2% of views on a phone (21,101 of 42,017) |

Rows three and four are the only ones a keepsake page answers cleanly. Row two is the one where it should not be attempted at all.

## What Indian law says about presents at a marriage

It is absent from every page ranking for this keyword, and the most useful thing an Indian reader can know before giving an envelope.

The [Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961](https://indiacode.gov.in/handle/123456789/523527), enacted 20 May 1961, makes giving or taking dowry an offence. Section 3(2)(a) then exempts "presents which are given at the time of a marriage to the bride (without any demand having been made in that behalf)" — provided they are entered in a list kept under the rules.

Those rules exist. The [Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules, 1985](https://indiacode.gov.in/handle/123456789/507681), in force since 2 October 1985, require the bride to maintain the list of presents given to her and the bridegroom to maintain his.

Each list must be in writing, prepared at the time of the marriage or as soon as possible after it, and must carry a brief description of each present, its approximate value, the name of the giver, and that person's relationship to the bride or bridegroom. Both bride and bridegroom sign it.

Two things follow. The line the statute draws is demand, not value — an unsolicited present is in a different category from one that was asked for. And the rule speaks of presents at the time of the marriage, not the engagement, so a guest's sagai gift is not what this machinery was built for.

## How much to spend, and the direction people get it wrong

The instinct to under-spend is measurable, and it points the wrong way. In a 2025 experiment with 216 participants published in Psychology of China, only [22.22% of people in the giver role](https://www.sciscanpub.com/index/index/down_article/id/8096.html) picked the premium-priced item as the one that would move the recipient more, while 59.72% of people in the recipient role said it would move them more — reported at chi-square (1, N = 144) = 20.93, p < 0.001. Prompting givers to think about their own preferences as a recipient lifted their premium choice to 40.28%.

Read it carefully: it concerns a price rise on the same object, not spending more in general, and the sample was Chinese. What transfers is the direction of the error: givers assume the recipient discounts money spent, and recipients do not.

The other half of the answer is who you are to them. A survey experiment with 104 married and engaged people in Pakistan found that [whether gift-giving felt like obligation or pleasure](https://ramss.spcrd.org/index.php/ramss/article/download/654/653) turned on the giver's and the recipient's attachment anxiety — the recipient's anxiety being a significant moderator of the giver's sense of obligation — and not on the gift.

## When a shareable page is the wrong engagement gift

Three cases.

An engagement where the two families are exchanging presents formally. A link has nothing to enter on a written list, and the moment is not asking for sentiment.

An engagement party you are physically attending. Something to hand over beats something to open on a phone in a room full of relatives, and every marketplace in this search result can put an object in your hands by tomorrow. We cannot.

A recipient who is not comfortable on a smartphone. Half of all views here are on a phone, so a grandparent-facing gift is better printed. On privacy: 42.7% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,458 of 3,417), which helps when a page must stay unseen until the ceremony, though a password is one more thing to fumble.

One more honest limit. A study of wedding gift exchange among the peoples of Dagestan found that many gifts that were once symbolic have been replaced by money, and that the amounts rise year on year.

Cash is efficient and it is winning. A keepsake is what cash cannot do; it does not settle a family obligation.

The Act's 37 sections contain no betrothal or engagement provision.

Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, s.3(2)(a): s.3(1) does not apply to 'presents which are given at the time of a marriage to the bride (without any demand having been made in that behalf)', provided they are entered in a list maintained under the rules.

Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules, 1985 (G.S.R. 664(E)), in force 2 October 1985: the bride maintains the list of presents given to her and the bridegroom his; each list must be in writing, prepared at or soon after the marriage, and state a brief description of each present, its approximate value, the giver's name and relationship, signed by both bride and bridegroom.

Experiment with 216 participants (78 male, 138 female, mean age 30.04): only 22.22% of participants in the giver role chose the premium-priced item as the more moving gift, against 59.72% of participants in the recipient role; chi-square(1, N=144)=20.93, p<0.001. Prompting givers to consider their own recipient preferences raised premium choice to 40.28%.

Scenario-based survey experiment with 104 married and engaged individuals in Pakistan: the gift-giving obligation felt by anxious givers varied with the recipient's attachment anxiety, which was a significant moderator; giver avoidance showed no direct negative effect on gift-giving pleasure but a significant indirect effect through relationship satisfaction.

Ethnographic study of wedding gift exchange among the peoples of Dagestan: many wedding gifts that were formerly symbolic in character have today been replaced by money, and the amounts increase every year. (Abstract read; Russian full text not translated.)

Dropping it gives 'engagement-gift-couple', which reads as broken English and loses the exact-phrase match in the URL that items 14 and 15 depend on. auditReport.honestAssessment: The defensible reason to cite this over Wirecutter, Brides and Forbes is that it is the only page in the set that separates the guest's engagement gift from the one the bride and groom give each other, and the only one that quotes India's Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules, 1985 - the written, signed, itemised list the bride and the bridegroom must each keep of presents given at the time of the marriage. Brides.com does answer the etiquette question on a separate URL (1,493 words, four factors, ten ideas, event planners quoted), so the briefing's claim that nobody in this SERP answers etiquette is wrong; what is true is that it answers it for an American engagement party with a registry, cites no data, and never mentions a sagai. None of the five pages cites a single study or statute. Against that, brides.com, forbes.com and nytimes.com carry domain authority SubhSandesh does not have, and Amazon, Flipkart and Etsy own the transactional half of the SERP; on the head term this post will not displace them, and its realistic route in is the etiquette and sagai long tail. Four things I could not verify and therefore left out of the page: any specific sagai or roka gifting custom (who gives what to whom, shagun amounts, the auspicious rupee-ending-in-one convention, who sends sargi) - I found no citable source for any of these and the body asserts none; whether the engagement gift being smaller than the wedding gift is documented anywhere rather than merely conventional (the body says so explicitly); the Dagestan paper, whose Russian full text I did not translate - only the abstract, which is what the citation states; and SubhSandesh's own pricing, since the Pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so the post makes no cost claim of any kind even though cost is this reader's live question. Three better-fitting open-access peer-reviewed sources were surrendered rather than cited because onlinelibrary.wiley.com is closed at 4+ posts, and Unpaywall reports no alternative location for any of them: 10.1002/mar.21983 (suspicion of large gift expenditures undermines gift appreciation), 10.1002/mar.21790 (givers and recipients differ on digital versus physical gift cards) and 10.1002/jcpy.1446 (givers overestimate the relationship harm of a late gift) - exact fits for the budget, digital-gift and late-gift questions respectively, and the orchestrator may want to spend the domain here. Source-cap check against the nine sibling posts written in this batch: zero collisions - indiacode.gov.in, sciscanpub.com, ramss.spcrd.org and caucasushistory.ru each appear in one post only, and no domain in the batch reaches three posts. Ranking depends on authority and links and takes months.
